A1.justification: Both readable 10-page PDFs describe the same SandboxVLM work and support comparison of all included text, equations, figures, and tables. Neither contains an appendix; both refer to separate supplementary material not included in the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original SandboxVLM benchmark evaluations, backbone comparisons, and seven ablation settings in Section 4 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, backbone comparisons, and ablation results in Section 4 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same abstract control, proxy elevation, multi-view voting and clustering, and rendered-box reasoning procedure. PAGE-4D is mentioned as future work, not adopted into the method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate SAT-Real, SAT-Synth, BLINK spatial-relation and relative-depth tasks, EmbSpatial-Bench, and PhysBench. No dataset or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3, including MindJourney and the backbone baselines. Newly cited APC and PAGE-4D are not evaluated as comparison methods.

E3.justification: The SAT test/validation splits, synthetic-data subsampling description, backbone configurations, and GPT-5-mini SAT-Real ablation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same seven ablation settings and findings about multi-view information, textual versus visual representations, and 3D abstraction. Figure 4 shows the same examples.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the reported qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains SandboxVLM's 81.4% spatial average and 58.3% PhysBench score.

T1.justification: The task definition, Equations 1–8, cross-view agreement criterion, and bounding-box construction are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about abstract perception, training-free 3D reasoning, and improvements across benchmarks and backbones.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and the limitations concerning dynamic scenes and unmodeled physical properties remain unchanged. The added PAGE-4D citation supplies an example for the already proposed temporal/motion extension, without changing the limitation or argument.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain the same, including 30 proxy pixels per object per view and the 2-meter step-back view. Both defer further hyperparameters, prompts, and subsampling details to supplementary material.

R1.justification: v2 adds a sentence acknowledging APC's abstract perspective reasoning and cites PAGE-4D in related work and future work. It removes PointNet++ and adds the already-cited VGGT to the point-cloud discussion, modestly updating literature coverage.

P1.justification: A short APC description and limited future-work wording are added, alongside citation renumbering and the version/date update. Section order and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added prose produces small changes to column breaks and spacing, particularly on pages 3–5 and 8, with some reference reflow. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–3 retain their designs and captions.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves scholarly context by acknowledging APC's related perspective-reasoning approach and linking the existing dynamic-scene future-work direction to PAGE-4D. The method, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so the quality gain is limited.
